title: Days and parts of the day (Wochentage und Tageszeiten)
summary: Name the days and the parts of the day, say when you do things (am Montag, am Abend), from when to when (von ... bis), and start a sentence with the time.
goals: Name the days of the week
Say when: am Montag, am Abend, in der Nacht
Say from when to when: von neun bis fünf
Start a sentence with the time, with the verb second

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 7: Days and times (Tageszeiten, Am Sonntag koche ich)

points: The days: [[Montag]], [[Dienstag]], [[Mittwoch]], [[Donnerstag]], [[Freitag]], [[Samstag]], [[Sonntag]]. All are der. In some regions Saturday is [[Sonnabend]].
Saturday and Sunday together are [[das Wochenende]], the weekend.
Every Monday: add -s and write it small: [[montags]], [[dienstags]], [[mittwochs]].
Two everyday phrases: [[Schönes Wochenende!]] and [[Was machst du am Wochenende?]]

phrases.de: der Montag, der Dienstag, der Mittwoch

phrases.en: What are you doing at the weekend?

notes.extra: [[montags]], [[dienstags]] ... for every Monday, Tuesday, and [[Sonnabend]] for Saturday.

points: Parts of the day: [[der Morgen]], [[der Vormittag]] (late morning), [[der Mittag]] (noon), [[der Nachmittag]], [[der Abend]], [[die Nacht]], [[die Mitternacht]].
Two ways to say when: [[am Abend]] or [[abends]], [[am Morgen]] or [[morgens]], [[am Nachmittag]] or [[nachmittags]]. The night is different: [[in der Nacht]] or [[nachts]], and [[um Mitternacht]].
Start a sentence with the time, and the verb still comes second: [[Am Abend gehe ich einkaufen.]]
Days and times join into one word: [[Sonntagmorgen]], [[Montagabend]].
A good wish for the evening: [[Schönen Abend!]]

phrases.en: In the evening I go shopping.
In the evenings I play the guitar.

points: [[um]] goes with clock times, official and everyday: [[um neunzehn Uhr]], [[um halb zwölf]]. One part of the day takes it too: [[um Mitternacht]].
[[am]] (short for [[an dem]]) goes with dates ([[am siebzehnten November]]), days ([[am Sonntag]]), the weekend ([[am Wochenende]]) and parts of the day ([[am Abend]]).
Exceptions for the parts of the day: [[zu Mittag]] (at lunchtime), [[in der Nacht]], [[um Mitternacht]].
[[im]] (short for [[in dem]]) goes with months ([[im Januar]]) and seasons ([[im Sommer]]).
A year has no preposition, or [[im Jahr]]: [[Er ist 2010 in die USA geflogen.]] or [[im Jahr 2010]]. Never 'in 2010', as in English.

phrases.de: Der Unterricht beginnt um vierzehn Uhr.
Ich habe am siebzehnten November eine Prüfung.
phrases.en: I have an exam on 17 November.

phrases.de: Am Wochenende fahren wir nach München.
phrases.en: At the weekend we're going to Munich.

phrases.de: In der Nacht gab es ein Gewitter.
phrases.en: There was a thunderstorm in the night.

phrases.de: Im Januar ist es in Deutschland sehr kalt.
phrases.en: In January it's very cold in Germany.

phrases.de: Im Sommer fliegen wir nach Japan.
phrases.en: In summer we're flying to Japan.
The film starts in the evening.

notes.extra: Years: no preposition, or [[im Jahr]] plus the year.

sections.title: All days are der
sections.text:
Every day is masculine: [[der Montag]], [[der Sonntag]]. All end in -tag except [[Mittwoch]], which means 'mid-week'.

- *On* a day: [[am Montag]], [[am Samstag]].
- *Every* Monday: add -s and write it small: [[montags]] = on Mondays.
- [[am Wochenende]] = at the weekend. [[die Woche]] = the week.
- [[heute]] = today, [[morgen]] = tomorrow: [[Heute ist Montag. Morgen ist Dienstag.]]

sections.title: Days you already know
sections.text: Russian среда (Wednesday) comes from 'middle', just like [[Mittwoch]]. And [[Samstag]], Russian суббота and Armenian շաբաթ all go back to the same Hebrew word, Sabbath. In Armenian, շաբաթ also means 'week'; in German the week is a different word, [[die Woche]].

sections.title: in der Nacht, and Gute Nacht
sections.text:
Every part of the day takes [[am]], except the night: [[in der Nacht]]. The [[der]] is not a mistake: after [[in]], [[die Nacht]] becomes [[der Nacht]]. Unit 6 explains why; for now, learn [[in der Nacht]] as one chunk.

With [[heute]] and [[morgen]]: [[heute Abend]] = this evening, [[heute Morgen]] = this morning, [[morgen Abend]] = tomorrow evening. But tomorrow morning is [[morgen früh]], never 'morgen Morgen'.

Review (Unit 0): [[Guten Abend!]] is a hello in the evening. [[Gute Nacht!]] is only a goodbye, late at night or before bed.

sections.title: From ... to: von ... bis
sections.text:
[[von]] ... [[bis]] gives a stretch of time: [[Ich arbeite von neun bis fünf.]] [[Der Kurs ist von Montag bis Freitag.]]

[[bis]] alone means 'until': [[Bis morgen!]] = See you tomorrow! (literally: until tomorrow).

Shop doors show opening hours like this:
- [[Geöffnet: Montag bis Freitag, von neun bis achtzehn Uhr.]]
- [[Am Sonntag geschlossen.]]

On signs it's short: Mo-Fr 9-18 Uhr. Read it as [[Montag bis Freitag, neun bis achtzehn Uhr]].

sections.title: Sunday is quiet
sections.text: In Germany almost all shops are [[geschlossen]] on Sundays and public holidays. Bakeries open for a few hours, and shops in big train stations stay open. So do your shopping on Saturday.

sections.title: Time first, verb second
sections.text:
You know from Unit 1 that the verb is always in second place, even when something else comes first: [[In München wohne ich.]] [[Heute lerne ich Deutsch.]]

German loves to start with the time. The verb comes right after it, and [[ich]], [[du]] and the rest move behind the verb:
- [[Ich arbeite am Montag.]] or [[Am Montag arbeite ich.]]
- [[Ich habe morgen Zeit.]] or [[Morgen habe ich Zeit.]]
- [[Wir lernen am Abend Deutsch.]] or [[Am Abend lernen wir Deutsch.]]

One thing before the verb, never two: not 'Am Montag ich arbeite'.

items.en: In the evening I study German.

items.de: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag.
items.en: I work from Monday to Friday.
On Mondays I have a class.
items.note: einen: the Unit 2 chunk after haben

items.de: Guten Morgen! Guten Abend! Gute Nacht!
items.en: Good morning! Good evening! Good night!

items.de: Am Montag arbeite ich von neun bis fünf.
items.en: On Monday I work from nine to five.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: In the evening I study German.
items.explanation: am + part of the day: am Abend. At the start of the sentence: Am.

items.question: How do you say 'at night'?
items.explanation: All parts of the day take am, except the night: in der Nacht.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: On Saturday I have time.
items.explanation: The time comes first, then the verb (second place), then ich: Am Samstag habe ich Zeit.

items.question: It's 11 p.m. and you're leaving a friend's place. What do you say?
items.explanation: Gute Nacht is a goodbye late at night. Guten Abend is a hello in the evening.
